transcript: Part fantasy, part fever dream, Lights Out: Nat “King” Cole at New York Theatre Workshop is a look into the psyche of this groundbreaking musician on the night of his final broadcast. His TV show is being cancelled, and being one of the very first and few Black TV hosts at the time, it's no mystery as to why. I'm kind of struggling to describe the form of this piece as I'm still trying to figure out exactly what I saw. There's Nat King Cole, his inner thoughts or alter ego personified by Sammy Davis Jr, and various other people in his life played by a small but mighty ensemble. Nat’s partially envisioning how his final broadcast might go, and partially having a broader retrospective and introspective on his life and career. Even this kind of vague description doesn't capture the layers to this piece, but I think I need to chew on it some more, and I'd love to hear more reactions to it since this was the first preview. What I do know is that as a play with a lot of music, this show serves up a huge platter of incredible performances. Dulé Hill as Nat King Cole and Daniel J Watts as Sammy Davis Jr are outstanding, as are Kenita Miller and 12 year old Mekhi Richardson. There's tap dancing, vocals galore, fun crowd work, thought provoking commentary, and some truly intoxicating sequences that had me completely enraptured. Although I can't quite put my finger on it, I really enjoyed it and I would recommend going in with the intention to just experience it in the moment and worry about figuring it out afterwards. With that, another program for my collection.
